description: Schmitt trigger 4.5V~5.5V 8 1 8.5ns@5V,50pF TSSOP-20 Buffers, Drivers, Receivers, Transceivers RoHS
notes: SCOPE CHANGED by the move to a differential pair. The two WS2812 data lines now leave the controller as differential pairs from MAX3485 transceivers driven straight off 3.3 V GPIOs, so the level shifting for them has moved to the converter boards. The only 5 V logic left on the controller is the single status-LED chain. An octal buffer for one channel is overkill - a single-gate HCT buffer would do, though none surfaced in the JLCPCB assembly catalogue, so the octal may simply stay as the available option.
HCT inputs have TTL thresholds (~1.5 V), so a 3.3 V GPIO drives them as a valid high, and the output swings to the 5 V rail. Plain HC would not work: its threshold is 0.7 x VCC = 3.5 V.

RETIRED REASON: an earlier note said 'Needed because WS2812D-F8 VIH is 0.7 x VDD = 3.5 V on a 5 V module rail'. This board drives no WS2812 - the modules are reached through MAX3485 differential pairs and the level shift lives on the converter board. What this part actually buffers is the SK6812MINI-E status chain on the controller, VIH 0.65 x VDD = 3.25 V against a 3.3 V GPIO, i.e. 50 mV of margin.
Octal, so it covers both data channels with six spare - the status LED chain uses one of those.

Supply range 4.5-5.5 V. CORRECTION: an earlier note said the rail reaches 4.60 V worst case and is 'inside it'. Worked from the TPS54360B's Eq. 1 with the real inductor DCR it is 4.50 V at a 4.75 V bus - exactly ON the floor, not inside it. Tolerable only because this part drives the status LED chain: a marginal rail during the few seconds of the 5 V phase means the indicators may misbehave before negotiation, not that the board fails to start.
TERMINOLOGY: called a differential pair in the design docs. RS-485 line levels, but no RS-485 connector convention - the pair runs over two poles of a picoMAX next to power and ground.
SETTLED as U9 in the BOM: it drives the status chain only, one channel of eight. Oversized but it is what the assembly catalogue offers.

CORRECTION: the earlier RECONSIDER verdict said "the data path no longer needs it", which was true of the module data path - that moved to MAX3485 differential - but not of the status-LED chain, which is why the README carries it as settled. The note about covering both data channels with spare capacity is also obsolete for the same reason.

NOT DELETABLE BY ANY LED CHOICE. Three SK6812 variants were compared (C5149201, C2909058, C2890041) and every one wants VIH >= 0.6-0.65 x VDD, i.e. 3.0-3.25 V on a 5 V rail, against the ESP32-C6's guaranteed V_OH of 0.8 x VDD = 2.64 V. Even the most permissive is out of reach.
designVerdict: SELECTED as U9 - the SK6812 status chain needs 5 V logic from a 3.3 V GPIO. Oversized (octal, one channel used) but the cheapest available part that does the level shift.
